_comment: Drives test/klippy/multi_mcu_stm32_stm32.test under a two-renode multi-bridge fan-out (stm32f103 main + stm32f407 satellite). The runner spawns one renode_launcher.py instance per bridge, each loading its own platform .repl and firmware ELF. tick_mode lockstep: klippy broadcasts each `advance T` to both renode tick sockets and waits for both `done` replies, so the two MCU clocks stay aligned with klippy's reactor - in free-run the independent wall-clock-bound renode clocks drift enough that G28 trips the trsync watchdog ('Communication timeout during homing'). Verified 4/4 with the renode tick path (sentinel-delimited monitor round-trips). auto_trsync_trigger_ticks fires the X/Y/Z endstops after 100 step edges so G28 completes; all stepper pins are on [mcu] so the pusher routes step_trigger to the main bridge's control socket. Both axes home on the renode mcu, so under tick-mode lockstep the homing steps are delivered over the host<->mcu byte shuttle, whose latency in simulated time is coarse and load-jittery (~one reactor advance quantum) rather than the ~1ms of a real serial link. klippy's serialqueue pre-transmits a command only 100ms ahead of its clock, so under full-suite contention that lead used to be eaten and the mcu step queue underrun -> firmware shutdown 'Timer too close'. That is now fixed at the source: the reactor's tick lockstep flushes ready serial commands at each advance target before the mcu runs forward (serialqueue.c serialqueue_flush_ready), so commands arrive with their normal real-hardware lead and no serialqueue margin is widened. This test homes both axes on the renode mcu but is single-mcu, so it needs no trsync widening either; it gates reliably on the flush alone.
